OverallSampleSize_source_quote: A total of 101 patients completed the survey with an overall response rate of 48%.

GroupSampleSizes.source_quote: Of the 101 patients who completed the survey, 63 patients (62%) quit smoking prior to undergoing primary TJA.
Fifteen patients (15%) underwent TJA without smoking cessation.

In total, 23 patients did not undergo TJA (23%): 19 of 23 patients were unable to quit smoking and thus remained ineligible for surgery, 2 patients were able to quit smoking but were unable to achieve a goal BMI prior to surgery, and 2 patients were able to quit smoking and then deferred surgery.

SampleSizePatterns_source_quote: The data from this self-reported survey study demonstrate that most patients (62%) will quit smoking, if required, for an elective TJA.
SampleSizePatterns_value: Most survey respondents quit smoking prior to TJA (62%), while smaller proportions underwent TJA without smoking cessation (15%) or did not undergo TJA at all (23%), illustrating that the smoking cessation requirement significantly influences patient pathways.
